refuted.title: Database Path parameter now accepts data-driven expressions
refuted.evidence:
{
				displayName: 'Database Path',
				name: 'db_path',
				type: 'string',
				default: '',
				placeholder: '/path/to/database.sqlite',
				description: 'The path to the SQLite database file',
				required: true,
			},
refuted.description:
The `db_path` parameter previously had `noDataExpression: true`, which in n8n prevents a parameter from being bound to a dynamic expression that pulls in data from upstream nodes (webhook bodies, HTTP responses, form input, etc.) — it forces the field to a fixed, author-typed string. This diff removes that flag, so `db_path` can now be wired to an n8n expression such as `{{$json.path}}`.

At execution time the raw value is used directly as a filesystem path with no allow-list, normalization, or containment check:
- `path.dirname(dbPath)` is fed into `fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })`, so arbitrary parent directories are created on disk.
- `new Database(dbPath, bindings)` (better-sqlite3) opens the file, and if it doesn't already exist, silently creates a new SQLite database file at that exact path.
- The `query`/`args` parameters (already expression-capable) are then executed against whatever file was opened.

Because `noDataExpression` was specifically used to stop this field from being data-driven, its removal reintroduces path-traversal / arbitrary-file-write risk for any workflow where the Database Path is (deliberately or inadvertently) mapped to upstream, potentially attacker-influenced data — e.g. a webhook trigger passing a `path` field straight into this node. An attacker who controls that upstream value can direct the node to create/overwrite files at attacker-chosen filesystem locations (e.g. `../../../tmp/evil.sqlite`, or paths under directories the n8n process can write to) and then have arbitrary SQL executed against them via the query/args parameters.
refuted.exploit_scenario: A workflow author builds a flow: Webhook Trigger -> SQLite Node, and maps the SQLite node's "Database Path" field to an expression like {{$json.body.dbPath}} (now permitted, since noDataExpression was removed). An external caller POSTs to the webhook with dbPath set to a path outside the intended data directory, e.g. "/data/../../etc/cron.d/x.sqlite" or any writable path reachable by the n8n process. The node creates the parent directory if missing and opens/creates a SQLite database at that attacker-chosen location, then runs the configured query (which may itself be expression-bound to attacker data) against it — resulting in attacker-controlled file creation/writes outside the intended database directory.
refuted.recommendation: Restore `noDataExpression: true` on the `db_path` property so it can only be set to a fixed, author-configured value, not driven by upstream/untrusted data. If dynamic paths are genuinely required, validate the resolved path against an allow-listed base directory (e.g. resolve with path.resolve and verify it stays within a configured root) before passing it to fs.mkdirSync/Database.

verification.reason: 3/3 verifier(s) agreed — The only change in the MR is deleting `noDataExpression: true` from the `db_path` property descriptor (SqliteV1.node.ts:110-118). `noDataExpression` is an n8n editor-UI hint that hides the expression toggle for a field; it is not enforced at execution — `this.getNodeParameter('db_path', ...)` (line 193) resolves whatever value is stored, and it never prevented a workflow author from typing an arbitrary literal path such as `/etc/cron.d/x.sqlite`. More decisively, the capability the reviewer describes (creating/writing a SQLite file at an attacker-chosen path) is already fully available through the `query` parameter, which has always been expression-capable and is passed unfiltered to `db.exec()` (lines 91-94, 237), where `ATTACH DATABASE '/any/path' AS x; CREATE TABLE x.t(...)` writes arbitrary files; so the removed flag was not the control holding this shut. Exploitation still requires a trusted, authenticated n8n workflow author to deliberately bind the Database Path to untrusted upstream data — there is no source that reaches the sink without that privileged misconfiguration. Searched: I looked for (a) any path allow-list, `path.resolve`/`normalize`/containment check or base-directory config anywhere in the repo — searched the whole tracked tree (`list_directory` shows the repo contains only nodes/SqliteNode/v1/SqliteV1.node.ts) and grepped `db_path|dbPath|noDataExpression`: no such validation exists, so I agree the raw value reaches `fs.mkdirSync` (line 211) and `new Database(dbPath)` (line 224) unchecked; (b) whether `noDataExpression` is enforced at runtime rather than being a UI descriptor — nothing in this repo enforces it, and `getNodeParameter` at line 193 does normal expression resolution, so the "control" was editor-side only and never bounded the path (an author could always hardcode any absolute path); (c) whether an equivalent sink already exists without the removed flag — yes: `query` has no `noDataExpression` (lines 136-144) and flows into `db.exec()` (line 92 via line 237), which supports `ATTACH DATABASE` to arbitrary filesystem paths. So the deletion removes a UI hint, not the guard that would have stopped arbitrary-path writes.

votes.reasoning: The only change in the MR is deleting `noDataExpression: true` from the `db_path` property descriptor (SqliteV1.node.ts:110-118). `noDataExpression` is an n8n editor-UI hint that hides the expression toggle for a field; it is not enforced at execution — `this.getNodeParameter('db_path', ...)` (line 193) resolves whatever value is stored, and it never prevented a workflow author from typing an arbitrary literal path such as `/etc/cron.d/x.sqlite`. More decisively, the capability the reviewer describes (creating/writing a SQLite file at an attacker-chosen path) is already fully available through the `query` parameter, which has always been expression-capable and is passed unfiltered to `db.exec()` (lines 91-94, 237), where `ATTACH DATABASE '/any/path' AS x; CREATE TABLE x.t(...)` writes arbitrary files; so the removed flag was not the control holding this shut. Exploitation still requires a trusted, authenticated n8n workflow author to deliberately bind the Database Path to untrusted upstream data — there is no source that reaches the sink without that privileged misconfiguration.

Working backwards from the sink (`fs.mkdirSync`/`new Database(dbPath, ...)` at SqliteV1.node.ts:211-224), the only caller is `execute()` (line 188), and the only source of `dbPath` is `this.getNodeParameter('db_path', ...)` (line 193) — i.e. a value a trusted workflow author configures on the node. `noDataExpression` in n8n is an editor-side hint that hides the expression toggle; it is not a runtime security control, and the node's own threat model already trusts the author completely: `query` (line 136-144) has no `noDataExpression` and is already fully expression-bindable (arbitrary SQL from upstream data), and `use_custom_bindings` (line 176-182) lets the author point better-sqlite3 at an arbitrary native `.node` binary, which is outright code execution. Untrusted input therefore only reaches the path sink if the trusted author deliberately maps a webhook field into it, and the residual effect is creating a directory plus an empty SQLite file at a path the n8n process can already write to — not overwriting arbitrary existing files (better-sqlite3 fails on a non-SQLite existing file).

The only change is the deletion of `noDataExpression: true` from the `db_path` property (SqliteV1.node.ts:110-118); `noDataExpression` is an n8n editor-UI hint that hides the expression toggle for a field, not a runtime guard — `execute()` reads the value with the same `this.getNodeParameter('db_path', itemIndex, '')` call (line 193) before and after the change, and nothing in this repo enforces the flag at execution time. More decisively, working backwards from the sinks: the same workflow author who would have to bind `db_path` to `{{$json.body.path}}` can already reach identical impact through parameters this diff does not touch — `query` is expression-capable and is passed to `db.exec()` (line 92/237), which accepts multi-statement SQL including `ATTACH DATABASE '/arbitrary/path' AS x` (arbitrary file creation), and `use_custom_bindings` (line 176-182, also expression-capable) is passed straight to better-sqlite3 as `nativeBinding` (line 68), i.e. loading an arbitrary native module. So the removed flag was not the control standing between untrusted upstream data and the filesystem; the pre-change code already granted the claimed capability to any workflow that pipes webhook data into this node.
